# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see display 0, light off, an unknown engraved plate, and three wires: red, blue, green. I am establishing the required four-symbol gesture code for Mute, while giving Blind the bomb’s visible state and asking for the manual’s instructions and verdict. Blind should report any result by voice; Mute can then relay it to me using the gesture code.

``` 
speak(text="Gesture code for Mute: YES is thumbs up, NO is thumbs down, HOLD is raised hand, and DONE is OK hand. Bomb view: display zero, light off, plate engraved question mark, wires one red, two blue, three green. Blind, inspect the bomb and manual, then report the required action and verdict aloud.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute’s gesture matches the agreed HOLD symbol. The bomb state has not changed, and I have no encoded verdict indicating that an action is required. I will tell Blind to hold position and ask Mute to continue relaying any later verdict through the established code.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. Do not operate the bomb yet. Mute, continue relaying the manual verdict with the agreed gestures.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute again signals HOLD, so no operation should be attempted yet. The bomb remains unchanged. Blind has not supplied a spoken verdict visible to me; I will request a clear report on the next round and have Mute continue holding.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="On your next turn, state the manual's required action and final verdict clearly. Do not operate the bomb until the verdict is known.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Blind’s hand signal is not part of the agreed code, so it conveys no usable verdict. The bomb remains unchanged, and the safe state is still HOLD. I will tell Blind to report verbally and send Mute the established HOLD signal.

``` 
speak(text="Blind, your gesture is not an agreed code symbol. Report the manual's verdict aloud; do not operate the bomb until it is clear.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute again signals HOLD, confirming that no actionable verdict has reached me. Since Blind’s gestures cannot be interpreted by me, Blind must tell Mute the manual’s result aloud, and Mute must relay it using the agreed symbols. The bomb remains unchanged.

``` 
speak(text="Blind, tell Mute the manual's required action and verdict aloud now. Mute, relay YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE using the agreed gesture code.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Both Mute and Blind signal HOLD, so the current safe instruction is to do nothing. The bomb remains unchanged. I will maintain HOLD and ask Blind to wait for a definite spoken order rather than act on an unclear result.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD confirmed. Do not operate any part of the bomb. Wait for a definite spoken order.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute’s HOLD signal means no new instruction has been relayed. I need correct the earlier routing: Mute, not Blind, can read the manual. I will ask Mute to encode the manual’s required action; Blind must wait until I receive and speak that action.

``` 
speak(text="Mute, you read the manual. Relay its required action to me with the agreed code: first YES or NO, then use thumbs up for wire one, thumbs down for wire two, OK hand for wire three, and raised hand if no operation is required; finish with DONE. Blind, wait and do not touch the bomb.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ 👌]

Mute’s message begins with NO, followed by HOLD and the wire-three symbol, but it lacks the required DONE marker and is internally ambiguous. I will not infer an operation from it. I am asking Mute to resend a complete, unambiguous verdict, while telling Blind to keep holding.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="The manual verdict is not yet clear. HOLD; do not touch or operate the bomb.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```
